articles.title: Help EFF Solve an Issue That's Bigger than Creepy Ads
articles.summary: Microsoft drops 167 vulnerabilities in April including a SharePoint zero-day and the deliciously named 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender bug. Meanwhile Chrome quietly patches its fourth zero-day of the year because Google's security team apparently never sleeps.

articles.title: Researchers uncover YellowKey and GreenPlasma Windows Zero-Days
articles.summary: Microsoft Exchange gets pwned via crafted email because apparently we're still living in 2003. CVE-2026-42897 is actively exploited in the wild, proving once again that email remains humanity's greatest security mistake.

articles.title: Pwn2Own Berlin 2026, Day One: $523,000 paid out, AI products fall
articles.summary: Researcher 'Nightmare-Eclipse' drops two fresh Windows zero-days targeting BitLocker and CTFMON framework. YellowKey and GreenPlasma sound like rejected Pokemon names but they'll ruin your encryption just fine.

articles.title: Internal Pentagon Report Reveals Hegseth Is Willfully Putting Civilians in Danger
articles.summary: Another CVSS 10.0 Cisco SD-WAN vulnerability gets exploited in the wild because apparently the first maximum severity bug wasn't enough excitement for one year. Cisco's network gear remains the gift that keeps on giving.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas education platform gets ransomwared, disrupting schools nationwide when attackers deface login pages with extortion demands. Nothing says 'back to school' like having your coursework held hostage by cybercriminals.

articles.title: On-Prem Microsoft Exchange Server CVE-2026-42897 Exploited via Crafted Email
articles.summary: OpenAI employees get pwned via TanStack supply chain attack because even AI overlords can't escape basic npm package poisoning. Two corporate devices compromised but hey, at least GPT-5 is still safe.

articles.title: CISA Adds Cisco SD-WAN CVE-2026-20182 to KEV After Admin Access Exploits
articles.summary: Foxconn factories across the US get breached with files from Apple, Intel, Google, Dell and NVIDIA allegedly stolen. When your manufacturing partner becomes a one-stop shop for industrial espionage, it's time to reconsider those supply chain contracts.

articles.title: Victory! End-to-End Encrypted RCS Comes to Apple and Android Chats
articles.summary: Instagram quietly kills its end-to-end encryption feature after years of promising privacy by default across Meta platforms. Another broken promise from Zuckerberg's surveillance empire masquerading as social media.

articles.title: EFF Launches New Offline Campaign for Saudi Wikipedian Osama Khalid
articles.summary: Victory as Apple finally enables end-to-end encryption for RCS messaging with Android in iOS 26.5. Only took a decade of public shaming but cross-platform encrypted messaging is finally here.

articles.title: The Boring Stuff is Dangerous Now
articles.summary: EFF launches campaign for Saudi Wikipedian Osama Khalid, who started contributing to Wikipedia Arabic at age 12 and became a prolific blogger advocating for open source technology. Digital freedom fighters start young in the Kingdom.
